title: Ireland Civil Society Fund 2027: Up to €800,000 Per Year for Overseas Development Projects
summary: The Government of Ireland’s Civil Society Fund 2027 is now open, offering substantial grant funding to eligible civil society organisations implementing overseas development projects. Through the fund, the Department of Foreign Affairs can provide up to 100% of eligible annual project costs , with grants of up to €800,000 per year for projects lasting as long as five years . The Civil Society Fund is designed to support development interventions delivered by civil society organisations and aligned with Ireland’s international development priorities. The programme also recognises the importance of sustained responses to long-term humanitarian crises, although sudden-onset acute emergency responses are not eligible. The 2027 call involves a two-stage application process . Organisations must first establish their eligibility and, if eligible, will subsequently receive the full application form. Irish-based organisations that believe they meet the requirements are required to submit an Eligibility Form by 5pm on Friday, 11 September 2026 . Eligible organisations will then be invited to submit the full application by 5pm on Monday, 2 November 2026 . Ireland Civil Society Fund 2027 at a Glance Opportunity Details Programme Civil Society Fund 2027 Funder Government of Ireland / Department of Foreign Affairs Implementing department Development Cooperation and Africa Division Opportunity type Overseas development grant Maximum funding Up to €800,000 per annum Maximum project duration Up to five years Funding level Up to 100% of annual project costs for successful applications Eligible applicants Irish civil society organisations and specifically invited international civil society organisations Application structure Eligibility Form followed by full application for eligible organisations Initial eligibility deadline 5pm, Friday, 11 September 2026 Full application deadline 5pm, Monday, 2 November 2026 Eligibility notification Late September 2026 Appraisal period December 2026/January 2027 Funding decisions March/April 2027 Project focus Overseas development projects Long-term humanitarian crises Eligible Sudden-onset acute emergency responses Not eligible What Is the Civil Society Fund? The Civil Society Fund (CSF) is a funding mechanism through which the Government of Ireland supports civil society organisations implementing overseas development projects. The fund provides financial support for organisations undertaking development work outside Ireland and is intended for interventions that contribute to international development objectives. Rather than being an individual funding opportunity, this is an organisational grant programme . Applications are submitted by qualifying civil society organisations rather than individuals. For successful applicants, the Department can fund up to 100% of annual project costs , subject to the applicable grant ceiling and other requirements. The maximum grant available is €800,000 per annum , while projects can have a duration of up to five years . This means that organisations selected for multi-year support could potentially receive significant funding over the life of a project, although the exact amount awarded will depend on the approved project, annual costs, funding conditions and assessment process. What Does the Civil Society Fund Support? The fund is intended to support overseas development projects implemented by eligible civil society organisations. The programme is therefore particularly relevant to organisations that already have the capacity, experience and institutional structures necessary to design and implement development interventions outside Ireland. Potential applicant organisations should carefully examine the official 2027 Call for Applications to determine whether their proposed intervention fits within the fund s specific policy priorities, geographic requirements and thematic criteria. The fund is not simply a general-purpose organisational funding programme. Applicants must propose eligible development interventions and satisfy the requirements established in the official call. Up to €800,000 Per Year in Grant Funding One of the most significant features of the Civil Society Fund is its maximum funding level. Successful applicants can receive: Up to €800,000 per year The fund can also support projects lasting: Up to five years The Department states that, for successful applications, it will fund up to 100% of annual project costs , up to the maximum grant limit. This can provide eligible civil society organisations with substantial resources to implement development programmes over an extended period. However, organisations should not interpret the €800,000 figure as an automatic award. It is the maximum available grant per annum , and funding decisions will depend on the quality, relevance, eligibility and assessment of each application. Important Organisational Income Requirement Applicants should pay particular attention to the Civil Society Fund s organisational income requirement. Income received from the Department, whether directly or indirectly, must not exceed 49% of the applicant organisation s overall income . The calculation is based on an average of the organisation s published audited accounts over the previous three years . Importantly, in-kind income is excluded from this calculation. This requirement means organisations should review their financial records before proceeding with an application. An organisation that relies too heavily on income from the Department of Foreign Affairs may not satisfy this particular eligibility requirement. Applicants should therefore examine their audited accounts for the relevant three-year period and calculate the proportion of overall organisational income originating directly or indirectly from the Department. Long-Term Humanitarian Crises Are Eligible The Civil Society Fund makes an important distinction between long-term humanitarian crises and sudden-onset emergencies. Interventions addressing long-term humanitarian crises can be eligible for support. This creates an opportunity for organisations working on sustained humanitarian challenges where development and humanitarian needs persist over an extended period. However, the fund does not support responses to sudden-onset acute emergencies. Therefore, organisations proposing projects should distinguish clearly between: Long-term humanitarian crises requiring sustained interventions; and Sudden-onset emergencies requiring immediate emergency response. A proposal focused primarily on responding to a newly occurring acute emergency would not meet this aspect of the fund s eligibility. Who Can Apply? The Civil Society Fund is primarily open to Irish civil society organisations that meet the eligibility criteria set out in the 2027 Call for Applications. The opportunity also allows for participation by a limited number of international civil society organisations , but there is an important restriction. International organisations cannot simply apply independently because they discover the call. The Government states that a limited number of international civil society organisations may be invited to the Civil Society Fund each year, based on policy priorities. Therefore: Irish-based civil society organisations that meet the requirements can proceed through the published eligibility process. International civil society organisations are eligible only if specifically invited . An international organisation that has not been invited should not assume that it can submit an application. This distinction is particularly important for NGOs and development organisations based in Africa, Asia, Latin America and other regions. Can African NGOs Apply? African civil society organisations should not assume that the Civil Society Fund is an open global grant competition. The official information specifically states that a limited number of international civil society organisations may be invited each year. Therefore, an African NGO, for example, would need to determine whether it has been specifically invited to participate in the 2027 Civil Society Fund. Being an NGO, having a strong development project or operating in a country relevant to international development does not, by itself, establish eligibility under the international-organisation provision. Potential international applicants should consult the official 2027 Call for Applications and use the contact details provided by the Department if they need clarification. Eligibility Is the First Stage The Civil Society Fund uses a staged application process. Organisations do not immediately submit the full grant application. Instead, eligible Irish-based organisations begin by completing an Eligibility Form . This first stage allows the Department to determine whether the organisation meets the basic requirements before inviting it to submit the full application. This means organisations should treat the Eligibility Form as an important part of the application process rather than as a simple registration exercise. First Deadline: Eligibility Form Irish organisations that intend to apply must submit their completed Eligibility Form to the Civil Society Fund mailbox by: 5pm on Friday, 11 September 2026 This is the first major deadline. Organisations should not wait until the final day because they need to gather supporting documents and ensure that the submission is complete. The Department specifically requests that applicants also provide supporting documentation, including: A Tax Clearance Certificate or equivalent Accounts for the last three years Relevant safeguarding policies The Eligibility Form and supporting documents should therefore be prepared together. What Happens After the Eligibility Form? Organisations that submit a completed Eligibility Form will be notified about their eligibility in late September 2026 . Organisations determined to be eligible will then receive the full application form by email. This creates a two-stage process: Stage 1: Eligibility Submit: Completed Eligibility Form Tax Clearance Certificate or equivalent Three years of accounts Safeguarding policies Deadline: 5pm, 11 September 2026 Stage 2: Full Grant Application If the organisation is confirmed as eligible, the Department will email the full application form. The completed application must then be submitted by: 5pm on Monday, 2 November 2026 Applicants should understand that submitting the Eligibility Form does not automatically mean that the organisation will be invited to submit a full proposal. The organisation must first be assessed as eligible. Second Deadline: Full Application The full application deadline is: 5pm on Monday, 2 November 2026 The Department states that applications received after the relevant deadlines will not be considered . Organisations should therefore plan backwards from the deadline and leave sufficient time for: Internal review Financial verification Safeguarding review Senior management approval Legal review where necessary Final editing Submission Printing and signing of the required hard copy Hard Copy Submission Requirement The application process also includes a subsequent hard-copy submission. After submitting the application form, applicants must submit a hard copy of the application form , signed by the legal representative of the organisation. The hard copy should be sent to: Civil Society Fund Civil Society Unit Development Cooperation and Africa Division Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade Riverstone House 23–27 Henry Street Limerick V94 R7YE Ireland Organisations should therefore allow sufficient time for the physical document to reach the Department after completing the electronic application requirements. Safeguarding Requirements Safeguarding is an important component of the eligibility documentation. Applicants are required to provide their safeguarding policies alongside the Eligibility Form. This is particularly relevant because organisations receiving development funding may work directly with: Children Women and girls People experiencing poverty Displaced populations Refugees People with disabilities Communities affected by conflict Other vulnerable or marginalised groups Organisations should ensure that their safeguarding policies are current, formally approved and appropriate to the nature of their proposed development work. Financial Documentation Applicants must also provide accounts covering the last three years . These documents are important for demonstrating the organisation s financial position and for assessing compliance with the Civil Society Fund s income requirements. Organisations should ensure that their accounts are: Complete Published or formally audited where required Consistent across the relevant three-year period Readily available for submission Compatible with the information provided in the Eligibility Form Financial information should be carefully checked before submission because discrepancies between the eligibility form and financial statements could create problems during assessment. Tax Clearance Applicants must include a Tax Clearance Certificate or equivalent with their eligibility submission. This is another indication that the fund is designed for established organisations with appropriate financial and legal structures. Organisations should verify that their tax documentation is valid and meets the Department s requirements before submitting the Eligibility Form. Application Assessment Timeline Following the application process, the Department intends to assess applications during: December 2026 and January 2027 Funding decisions are expected to be communicated in: March/April 2027 The timeline therefore provides applicants with several months between the full application deadline and the expected funding decision. However, organisations should not assume that funding will be available before the official notification of a decision. Important Application Rules Applicants should pay close attention to the Department s procedural requirements. Late applications are not accepted The Department states that forms received after the relevant deadlines will not be considered. This applies to the relevant stages of the process, so applicants should submit their documents before the stated closing times. Individual meetings are not available Once the Call for Applications is issued, representatives of applicant organisations cannot request individual meetings concerning the application form until funding decisions have been communicated. This means organisations should rely on the official documentation and the designated Civil Society Fund contact channel for questions. Attempts to influence the decision can lead to disqualification The Department explicitly states that any attempt to influence the outcome of the decision-making process in relation to grant applications will result in disqualification . Applicants should therefore maintain a professional and transparent application process and avoid inappropriate attempts to influence officials or the assessment process. Organisations based in Ireland that consider they meet the criteria set out in the 2027 Call for Applications and who wish to apply for funding can download an Eligibility Form . How Organisations Should Prepare Although applicants should rely on the official call for the complete requirements, organisations can begin preparing immediately. 1. Review the eligibility requirements Start by reading the full 2027 Call for Applications carefully. Do not begin with the project narrative before confirming that the organisation itself is eligible. 2. Review three years of financial records Check the organisation s published audited accounts for the relevant three-year period. Calculate the proportion of organisational income received directly or indirectly from the Department to determine whether the organisation satisfies the 49% income requirement . 3. Prepare safeguarding documentation Make sure safeguarding policies are current and can be provided with the Eligibility Form. 4. Confirm tax clearance Obtain the relevant Tax Clearance Certificate or equivalent documentation. 5. Examine the proposed development project The project should clearly correspond to the objectives and eligibility requirements of the Civil Society Fund. Organisations should be able to explain: What development problem they are addressing Where the project will operate Who will benefit Why the intervention is necessary What outcomes are expected How activities will produce those outcomes How progress will be measured How the intervention will be sustained How risks will be managed Why the organisation is appropriately positioned to implement it 6. Build a realistic budget Because funding can cover up to 100% of annual project costs for successful applications, organisations should prepare a realistic and well-supported project budget. The budget should correspond directly with the activities and expected results of the project. 7. Plan for a multi-year intervention where appropriate Projects can last for up to five years. Organisations with interventions requiring sustained implementation should consider how activities, outcomes, partnerships and financing would develop over the full project period. 8. Begin internal approvals early The application may require approval from senior management, a board, legal representatives or other authorised personnel. Organisations should therefore avoid leaving internal approval until the final days before submission. Why the Civil Society Fund Is Significant The scale and duration of the Civil Society Fund make it potentially valuable for established development organisations. A maximum annual grant of €800,000 provides considerably more funding capacity than many small community or seed grants. The possibility of funding projects for up to five years also makes the programme relevant to interventions that require long-term implementation rather than short-term activities. Longer-term development programmes may involve: Institutional strengthening Community development Capacity building Education Health Gender equality Poverty reduction Governance Human rights Livelihood development Resilience building Long-term humanitarian support However, the specific thematic and geographic priorities of the 2027 call should always be checked before preparing a proposal. Important Distinction: Grant Funding vs Individual Funding This opportunity is a grant for civil society organisations , not an individual scholarship or fellowship. Individuals cannot apply for the €800,000 grant as individuals. Similarly, students, job seekers and individual researchers should not treat the Civil Society Fund as a personal funding programme. The applicant is the eligible organisation , which must demonstrate the institutional, financial, legal and safeguarding capacity required by the programme. What International Organisations Should Know International civil society organisations should pay particular attention to the invitation requirement. The Government of Ireland states that only a limited number of international civil society organisations may be invited each year. Eligibility is determined according to policy priorities, and only organisations specifically invited are eligible to apply. Therefore, international NGOs should not assume that the publication of the call means that every international organisation worldwide can submit an application. This is especially important for organisations headquartered outside Ireland. Geographic Eligibility The Civil Society Fund supports overseas development projects , meaning the programme is relevant to development activities implemented outside Ireland. The official page also provides an OECD DAC Country Codes / ODA recipients resource as one of the key documents for the call. Organisations should consult the official 2027 Call for Applications and the OECD DAC list to determine whether their proposed project location meets the relevant development-assistance requirements. For African organisations, geographic relevance should therefore be assessed alongside the separate requirement concerning whether an international organisation has been specifically invited. Key Documents Applicants should review the official programme documents before preparing their submission. The key documents include: 2027 Call for Applications OECD DAC Country Codes / ODA Recipient List 2027 Civil Society Fund Eligibility Form The official Civil Society Fund webpage also provides access to these documents and additional programme information. Application Deadlines There are two critical deadlines for the 2027 Civil Society Fund. Eligibility Form 5pm, Friday, 11 September 2026 This is the deadline for eligible Irish-based organisations to submit the completed Eligibility Form and required supporting documents. Full Application 5pm, Monday, 2 November 2026 Only organisations that are confirmed as eligible will receive the full application form and proceed to this stage. Organisations should not confuse the two deadlines. The 11 September 2026 deadline is the first-stage eligibility deadline , while 2 November 2026 is the deadline for the full application . Key Takeaways for Prospective Applicants Before applying, organisations should remember the following: The Civil Society Fund supports overseas development projects . It is an organisational grant , not an individual funding opportunity. Successful projects can receive up to €800,000 per year . Projects can run for up to five years . The Department can fund up to 100% of annual project costs , subject to the grant limit and applicable conditions. Departmental income must not exceed 49% of the applicant organisation s overall income , calculated using the average of published audited accounts over three years. Long-term humanitarian crisis interventions are eligible. Sudden-onset acute emergency responses are not eligible. Irish civil society organisations can apply if they meet the requirements. International civil society organisations must be specifically invited to apply. The first stage requires an Eligibility Form. Applicants must provide financial accounts, tax clearance documentation and safeguarding policies. The Eligibility Form deadline is 5pm, 11 September 2026 . Eligible organisations will be notified in late September 2026 . The full application deadline is 5pm, 2 November 2026 . Applications received after the relevant deadlines will not be considered. Appraisal is expected in December 2026/January 2027 . Funding decisions are expected in March/April 2027 . A signed hard copy of the application must subsequently be submitted to the Civil Society Fund in Limerick. Attempts to influence the funding decision can result in disqualification. Conclusion The Ireland Civil Society Fund 2027 represents a significant funding opportunity for eligible civil society organisations implementing overseas development projects. With grants of up to €800,000 per annum , the possibility of projects lasting up to five years , and funding of up to 100% of annual project costs , the programme can provide substantial support for well-designed and strategically relevant development interventions. However, organisations should pay close attention to the eligibility conditions. The opportunity is primarily available to Irish civil society organisations , while only a limited number of international civil society organisations specifically invited by the Government of Ireland may apply. It is therefore not an open global grant competition for every NGO. The application process has two important stages. Irish organisations intending to apply must first submit the Eligibility Form and required documentation by 5pm on Friday, 11 September 2026 . Organisations that are confirmed as eligible will receive the full application form and must submit it by 5pm on Monday, 2 November 2026 . Prospective applicants should begin preparations early by reviewing the official call, checking their financial eligibility, preparing their three years of accounts, confirming tax clearance, reviewing safeguarding policies and developing a strong project concept aligned with the fund s requirements. The Civil Society Fund can be particularly valuable for established organisations seeking substantial, multi-year support for overseas development work, but applicants should carefully verify all eligibility, thematic, geographic and financial requirements in the official 2027 Call for Applications before submitting. title: Lisbon AI Safety Hub Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship 2026: 8-Week In-Person Programme in Portugal for Students and Working Professionals.
summary: The Lisbon AI Safety Hub (LAISH) is inviting students and working professionals to apply for its Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship , an eight-week programme designed to introduce participants to the rapidly developing field of artificial intelligence safety and help them identify meaningful ways to contribute to the safe development and governance of advanced AI. Based in Lisbon, Portugal, the Lisbon AI Safety Hub is building a community that brings together researchers, academics, policymakers and ambitious individuals who want to contribute to the development of safe and responsibly governed artificial intelligence. The fellowship provides an opportunity for participants who may not have a technical background in artificial intelligence to understand the opportunities and risks associated with increasingly capable AI systems. Through the programme, participants will explore AI safety, understand major risks associated with advanced AI, examine governance approaches and consider practical career and professional pathways through which they can contribute to the field. Applications for the current fellowship cohort opened on August 1 , with applications closing on September 30 . The cohort is scheduled to begin on October 6 . About the Lisbon AI Safety Hub The Lisbon AI Safety Hub is a community-focused organisation working to help Portugal play a meaningful role in the development of advanced artificial intelligence and the emerging global AI safety field. The organisation brings together people from different professional and academic backgrounds, including: Researchers Academics Policymakers Students Technology professionals Individuals interested in AI safety and governance People looking for ways to contribute to the responsible development of advanced AI LAISH takes a broad view of AI safety. Rather than treating the subject purely as a technical computer science problem, the organisation describes AI safety as a sociotechnical problem , meaning that technical research, governance, institutions, policy and human decision-making all have important roles to play. Its goal is to help develop a community capable of contributing to safer AI development in Portugal and beyond. What Is AI Safety? Artificial intelligence systems are becoming increasingly capable and are being integrated into more areas of society, business, research and government. As AI capabilities increase, an important question arises: how can humans ensure that increasingly powerful AI systems remain aligned with human intentions, values and interests? AI safety broadly concerns the research, policies, institutions and practices needed to reduce the risks associated with advanced artificial intelligence. The Lisbon AI Safety Hub highlights three major areas of AI safety: 1. AI Alignment AI alignment focuses on ensuring that advanced AI systems pursue objectives that reflect what humans actually intend. A system may technically follow an instruction while still producing an outcome that humans did not want. Alignment research therefore examines how AI systems can better understand and follow human goals and intentions as their capabilities become more powerful. The fellowship introduces participants to the importance of alignment and the challenges involved in ensuring that increasingly capable systems remain under meaningful human direction. 2. AI Interpretability Interpretability focuses on understanding what is happening inside AI systems. Modern neural networks can be extremely complex, making it difficult for humans to understand precisely how they arrive at particular decisions or outputs. Interpretability research seeks to make these systems more understandable so researchers can potentially: Identify what AI systems have learned Understand how systems represent information Detect potential problems Predict certain types of failure Audit AI behaviour Intervene before problems become more serious Understanding how AI systems work internally is therefore an important part of developing safer and more reliable systems. 3. AI Governance AI governance concerns the rules, policies, institutions and international arrangements that influence how powerful AI systems are developed and deployed. Governance questions include: Who should be allowed to develop frontier AI? What safeguards should developers follow? What limits should apply to advanced AI systems? How should governments regulate powerful AI technologies? Who should be held accountable when AI systems cause harm? How can countries cooperate on AI safety? What institutions are needed to manage increasingly capable AI? The governance side of AI safety provides opportunities for people with backgrounds in areas such as public policy, law, international relations, economics, governance, communications and social sciences. About the Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship The Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship is a non-technical programme designed to give participants an introduction to AI risks and practical ways they can contribute to efforts to make advanced AI safer. Importantly, participants do not need prior technical knowledge to apply. The programme is structured to help participants progress from understanding the fundamental AI safety problem to considering how they personally might contribute. The fellowship covers four main areas. 1. Why AI Safety Matters Participants begin by developing an understanding of advanced artificial intelligence and why AI safety has become an increasingly important area of work. This includes exploring: The development of increasingly capable AI systems The potential benefits of advanced AI Potential risks associated with advanced AI Why AI safety is becoming increasingly important Why maintaining meaningful human control over powerful AI systems matters The aim is to provide participants with a foundation for understanding why AI safety is considered an important emerging field. 2. Understanding the Risks The fellowship then examines the different ways advanced artificial intelligence could affect individuals, institutions and society. Participants explore major categories of AI risk and learn how people working in the field think about and evaluate those risks. This part of the fellowship can help participants develop a more structured understanding of questions surrounding: AI reliability AI alignment AI system behaviour Societal impacts Risks associated with increasingly capable systems Potential failure modes The challenges of managing advanced AI Rather than requiring participants to already be experts, the programme provides an introductory pathway into these discussions. 3. Governance and Action Another major component of the fellowship focuses on governance. Participants examine how policy, institutions and international coordination can contribute to safer AI development. This is particularly relevant for individuals interested in careers involving: Public policy Technology policy Government International affairs Regulation Research Governance Responsible technology AI policy Institutional decision-making The governance component demonstrates that contributing to AI safety does not necessarily require becoming an AI engineer or machine-learning researcher. 4. Identifying Your Next Step The final component focuses on helping participants identify practical ways to contribute to AI safety. Participants are encouraged to consider how their existing skills, education, professional experience and interests could connect with opportunities in the field. Possible pathways may include: Career development Academic research Policy work Governance Technical research Community building Communications Advocacy Further study Work related to responsible AI This makes the fellowship relevant not only to people who are already working in artificial intelligence, but also to people considering a transition into the field. Fellowship Duration, Location and Important Dates The Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship has the following programme details: Programme: Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship Duration: 8 weeks Location: Lisbon, Portugal Format: In person Applications opened: August 1 Application deadline: September 30 Cohort starts: October 6 Target participants: Students and working professionals Technical prerequisites: No technical knowledge required Applicants should take note of the September 30 application deadline and submit their applications before the closing date. Who Should Apply? The fellowship is particularly relevant to students and working professionals who want to learn more about artificial intelligence safety and explore ways to contribute to the field. You may be a suitable candidate if you are: A student interested in AI Students who are curious about artificial intelligence, technology, research, policy or the societal effects of AI can use the fellowship to develop a foundational understanding of AI safety. The programme may also help students identify potential areas for further study or career development. A working professional considering a career transition Professionals from fields outside traditional artificial intelligence can explore how their existing skills could be applied to AI safety. For example, people with experience in policy, communications, research, governance, law, management, technology or other professional areas may find the programme useful. Someone interested in AI governance People interested in the rules and institutions surrounding artificial intelligence may particularly benefit from the governance component of the programme. This can be relevant to individuals interested in government, public policy, regulation, international cooperation and technology governance. Someone without a technical AI background One of the important features of the programme is that no technical knowledge is required . This means that applicants should not assume they need to be programmers, machine-learning engineers or AI researchers before they can participate. The fellowship is designed to provide an introduction to the field and help participants understand where their own skills and interests could fit. Why the Fellowship Is Important Artificial intelligence is developing rapidly, and increasingly capable systems are expected to influence many areas of society. This creates a growing need for people who can think about AI not only from a technical perspective but also from the perspectives of governance, policy, institutions and society. A field such as AI safety therefore requires people with different backgrounds and skill sets. The Lisbon AI Safety Hub s approach recognises this by supporting both technical and governance-oriented work . This broad perspective means that someone does not necessarily have to become a machine-learning researcher to contribute to AI safety. Instead, individuals may contribute through: Technical research Policy development Governance Regulation Academic research Institutional design Communications Community building International coordination Other professional areas connected to responsible AI development Other Ways to Get Involved With the Lisbon AI Safety Hub The fellowship is only one of several ways to engage with the Lisbon AI Safety Hub. Events and Lectures LAISH organises events designed to help grow the AI safety community. These include: Film screenings Directed discussion groups Community meetings Lectures from industry experts Research discussions Social events The organisation states that events are primarily held in English, although Portuguese speakers are expected to be present. Career Guidance LAISH also offers career guidance for individuals interested in working in AI safety. Participants can seek tailored advice about opportunities in the field and ways to develop a career that enables them to contribute to AI safety. This can be useful for people who understand that they are interested in the field but are unsure which professional or academic direction to take. Click HERE for more information. Newsletter The organisation publishes a newsletter covering topics such as: Frontier AI news Jobs Fellowships Opportunities within the AI safety field The newsletter is available in English and Portuguese. Community Discord LAISH also maintains a Discord community where people can connect with other members, exchange resources and receive information about events and community activities. This provides an additional way for people to remain connected to the AI safety community beyond individual programmes. What Makes This Fellowship Different? One of the strongest features of the Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship is its accessibility to people without technical AI expertise. Many emerging technology programmes focus heavily on programming, mathematics, machine learning or computer science. The Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship instead provides an introductory pathway that allows participants to understand the broader AI safety landscape before deciding how they might contribute. The programme combines: Understanding advanced AI Exploring AI risks Learning about AI governance Considering practical career pathways This makes it potentially valuable for people coming from different educational and professional backgrounds. Potential Career Directions After Learning About AI Safety Although participation in the fellowship does not automatically qualify someone for a particular job, developing knowledge of AI safety can help participants explore several career directions. Depending on their existing background and future training, participants may consider areas such as: AI policy Technology governance AI safety research AI governance research Public policy Responsible AI AI regulation Academic research Technology communications AI-related programme management International AI policy Community development Participants can also use the fellowship to determine whether they want to pursue more specialised technical or governance training. APPLY HERE. How to Apply Interested applicants should apply through the Lisbon AI Safety Hub s official fellowship application process. Applications for the current cohort opened on August 1 and close on September 30 . The programme begins on October 6 and lasts for eight weeks . Because the fellowship is listed as an in-person programme in Lisbon , applicants should carefully consider their ability to participate in the programme at the stated location. Applicants who have questions can contact the Lisbon AI Safety Hub at: contact@lisbonaisafetyhub.org Important Details at a Glance Opportunity: Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship Organisation: Lisbon AI Safety Hub (LAISH) Location: Lisbon, Portugal Programme format: In person Duration: 8 weeks Application opening date: August 1 Application deadline: September 30 Cohort start date: October 6 Who can apply: Students and working professionals Technical knowledge required: No Main areas: AI safety, AI risks, alignment, interpretability and governance Career focus: Identifying practical ways to contribute to AI safety Contact: contact@lisbonaisafetyhub.org Frequently Asked Questions Is the Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship a scholarship? No. Based on the information provided, this is a fellowship programme , not a scholarship. The provided information does not state that participants receive tuition funding, a stipend, travel support or other financial benefits. Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that the programme is fully funded unless LAISH confirms otherwise. Do I need to know programming to apply? No. The fellowship specifically states that no technical knowledge is required , making it accessible to people who do not have a technical AI or programming background. Who is the fellowship for? The programme is intended for students and working professionals who want to learn about AI safety and explore ways of contributing to the field. Do I need an AI degree? No specific AI degree is listed as a prerequisite. The programme is designed as an introduction to AI safety and does not require technical knowledge. Is the fellowship online? The fellowship is listed as in person in Lisbon, Portugal . Therefore, applicants should be prepared to participate physically in Lisbon. When does the application close? The application deadline is September 30 . When does the cohort begin? The cohort is scheduled to begin on October 6 . How long does the fellowship last? The programme lasts eight weeks . Can people from outside Portugal apply? The information provided does not specify a nationality or citizenship restriction. However, because the fellowship is listed as an in-person programme in Lisbon , international applicants should consider the practical requirements associated with participating in Portugal. Is technical AI knowledge required? No. The fellowship explicitly states that no technical knowledge is required . What areas of AI safety are covered? The programme introduces participants to why AI safety matters, the risks associated with advanced AI, governance and practical ways to contribute. The wider LAISH approach also highlights areas including alignment, interpretability and governance . Conclusion The Lisbon AI Safety Hub Foundations of AI Safety Fellowship provides an accessible entry point into one of the world s emerging technology fields. As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly capable, questions about how these systems can remain safe, reliable and subject to meaningful human direction are becoming increasingly important. Addressing these questions requires more than technical expertise alone. It also requires people who understand policy, governance, institutions, research, communication and the broader societal implications of AI. With its eight-week, in-person programme in Lisbon , the fellowship offers students and working professionals an opportunity to develop foundational knowledge of AI safety, explore the risks associated with advanced AI, understand governance approaches and consider practical ways to contribute to the field. The fact that no technical knowledge is required makes the programme particularly accessible to people who are interested in AI safety but do not come from a computer science or engineering background. For individuals interested in the future of artificial intelligence and the challenge of ensuring that increasingly powerful AI remains beneficial and responsibly governed, the programme could provide an important starting point. Applications opened August 1 and close September 30, with the next cohort scheduled to begin October 6. Applicants who are interested should review the official fellowship information carefully and submit their application before the deadline. For more OFY Fellowship opportunities, VISIT HERE. title: Alpha Fellowship 2026: Join a Breakout a16z Startup or Get Up to $250,000 to Build Your Own Company.
summary: Highly technical students and recent software engineering graduates looking for an opportunity to accelerate their careers in the startup ecosystem can apply for the Alpha Fellowship , a programme designed to place exceptional early-career engineers into full-time roles at fast-growing companies within the Andreessen Horowitz ecosystem or provide aspiring founders with capital to begin building their own company. The Alpha Fellowship is designed for ambitious technical builders who do not want to wait years before taking on meaningful responsibility. Participants can follow one of two pathways. The Startup Track connects successful fellows with fast-growing portfolio companies for full-time engineering positions that include salary and equity. The Founder Track is designed for individuals who want to build their own startup and provides early capital even when they do not yet have a formal company, established team or fully developed idea. Both pathways begin with an approximately two-month, eight-week, in-person fellowship experience that includes an immersive retreat, founder discussions, curated dinners, small-group conversations and opportunities to interact with engineers, startup founders, operators and investors. The programme also provides fellows with access to the broader a16z speedrun and EO Ventures communities and events . For applicants who want to work at a rapidly growing technology company, become a founder or gain exposure to experienced entrepreneurs and investors, Alpha offers a potentially significant early-career pathway. What Is the Alpha Fellowship? The Alpha Fellowship is an early-career programme focused on highly technical software engineers who have demonstrated an ability and desire to build. Its central proposition is straightforward: rather than waiting for an opportunity to emerge, technically strong students and recent graduates can use Alpha as a direct route into either a high-growth startup or entrepreneurship. The programme offers two main choices: Join a breakout portfolio company through the Startup Track. Start your own company through the Founder Track. The fellowship component provides an intensive in-person experience, while the two tracks provide different long-term outcomes. For Startup Track participants, the fellowship is combined with a full-time engineering position. For Founder Track participants, the fellowship is combined with the opportunity to build a startup and access early-stage funding. Who Is Alpha Looking For? Alpha is looking for people who are highly technical and have demonstrated that they can build. The programme specifically targets: Highly technical software engineers Exceptional students Recent graduates Recent graduates within approximately three years of leaving school People with a track record of building Individuals with strong technical curiosity People who want to move quickly into startups or entrepreneurship The programme is not designed as a general graduate fellowship for applicants from every professional background. It is specifically focused on software engineering talent. A Programme for Builders A central theme of Alpha is building. The programme is intended for people who do not simply want to learn about startups but want to participate directly in building products, companies and technology. For applicants joining the Startup Track, this means becoming a full-time engineer at a rapidly growing company. For Founder Track applicants, it means having the opportunity to begin building a company full-time. This makes Alpha particularly relevant to technically skilled individuals who want their early careers to involve substantial hands-on work. The Two Alpha Fellowship Tracks Startup Track: Join a Fast-Growing Portfolio Company The Startup Track is designed for technical students and recent graduates who want to gain experience inside a high-growth startup. Successful candidates can take full-time engineering roles at fast-growing companies within the a16z portfolio. The fellowship portion lasts approximately two months, but the employment opportunity continues beyond the fellowship. Fellows are hired directly by the matched company and continue in their full-time roles after the fellowship concludes. How Startup Matching Works The matching process is designed around mutual fit between candidates and participating companies. Candidates and companies rank their preferences, after which matches are made. If a candidate is matched with a company and accepts the opportunity, the fellow becomes an employee of that company. This is an important distinction: fellows who join startups are not employees of a16z simply because the company is part of the a16z portfolio. Instead, the successful fellow is hired directly by the participating company. Founder Track: Start Your Own Company The Founder Track is designed for technically strong individuals who want to become entrepreneurs. Its most distinctive feature is that applicants do not necessarily need to have already established a conventional startup. Alpha states that it is willing to back founders at an extremely early stage, including before they have: A legal entity A complete startup idea A founding team This makes the programme particularly interesting for technical builders who have the ambition to become founders but are still at the beginning of the process. Apply as an Individual Founder Track applicants apply individually. If an applicant already knows who they want to build a company with, each potential founder should submit their own application and identify the person or people they intend to build with. This means that an applicant does not need to wait until they have assembled a complete founding team before applying. Founder Track Funding The Founder Track provides significant early-stage financial support. Accepted founders receive an initial: $20,000 grant The programme also makes available: Up to $250,000 in total investment This gives accepted founders capital to begin working full-time on their company. The programme s stated timeline explains that accepted founders receive their initial $20,000 grant and begin working full-time on their idea, with up to $250,000 in total investment available. This is particularly significant because Alpha is willing to support founders at a stage when they may not yet have a traditional venture-backed startup. Potential Access to a16z Speedrun Alpha also provides a potential pathway into a16z speedrun , described by the programme as its flagship startup programme. Once Alpha fellows complete the fellowship with a team and company formed, they receive priority consideration for a16z speedrun. The programme states that speedrun can provide: Up to $1 million in investment For aspiring founders, this means Alpha can potentially serve as an early step in a larger startup-building and fundraising journey. The pathway can therefore look like: Apply to Alpha as a technical builder. Join the Founder Track if selected. Receive initial funding. Build a team and company. Complete the Alpha fellowship. Receive priority consideration for a16z speedrun. Potentially access further investment through speedrun. The Eight-Week In-Person Fellowship Both tracks include an approximately two-month, eight-week fellowship experience. The programme is conducted in person and is designed to surround fellows with experienced technical and startup leaders. The fellowship includes: An immersive kickoff retreat Curated dinners Founder AMAs Small-group discussions Conversations with engineering leaders Meetings with portfolio founders Interactions with investors Access to selected a16z speedrun events Participation in the broader startup community Rather than functioning solely as classroom-based training, the fellowship is designed around direct exposure to people building and funding technology companies. Founder AMAs and Community Events One of the programme s notable features is access to founder conversations. Fellows participate in founder AMAs, allowing them to learn directly from people who have built technology companies. They also gain opportunities to participate in small-group dinners and discussions with people working across the startup ecosystem. The objective is to give fellows exposure to the practical realities of building and scaling technology companies. Speakers and Mentors The Alpha Fellowship lists a range of technology founders, investors and leaders among its speakers and mentors. Previous Speakers The programme also highlights previous speakers associated with major technology companies. Career Opportunities Through the Startup Track For early-career software engineers, the Startup Track offers more than a short-term fellowship. This can provide experience in: Product development Software engineering Startup environments Rapid product iteration Working with technical teams Building products at high-growth companies Collaborating with founders and operators Because the role continues after the fellowship, fellows have the opportunity to build a longer-term career within their matched company. Salary and Equity Startup Track participants receive a full-time engineering position with: Salary Equity Compensation is determined by the hiring company. The Founder Opportunity For those who want to build rather than join an existing company, the Founder Track offers a different type of opportunity. Instead of being matched to an established startup, the participant works full-time on creating a company. The programme can support founders even before they have: Incorporated a company Developed a final product Built a team Fully defined the startup idea This makes the Founder Track particularly relevant to technical people who have strong entrepreneurial ambitions. Stage 4: The On-Ramp The fellowship begins with an immersive retreat. During the retreat, fellows meet one another and spend time with the a16z speedrun team. Stage 5: Fellowship Programming From the beginning of the fellowship through its completion, fellows participate in weekly small-group conversations with engineers, operators and investors. These conversations take place alongside the fellows normal full-time work. Stage 6: Completion The fellowship concludes with a capstone event. Fellows present to the a16z speedrun team and broader community. Startup Track fellows continue working in their full-time positions after the fellowship. Application Submit an application and be considered for the relevant cohort. 02. Interview and Assessment Complete the technical assessment and live interviews if selected. 03. title: EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027: UK Research Organisations Can Apply for Up to £62,500 to Host Policy Fellowships
summary: Applications are now open for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 , an initiative providing UK research organisations with funding of up to £62,500 to establish and deliver Policy Fellowship programmes for public and civil servants. The programme is designed to strengthen connections between the UK research community and the public sector by creating opportunities for public and civil servants to spend dedicated time engaging with academics and researchers on real-world policy challenges. Eligible research organisations across the United Kingdom can apply to EvEx to develop and run their own funded Policy Fellowship programme. Successful organisations will host Policy Fellows between January and May 2027 , providing opportunities for problem-solving, professional development, network building, knowledge exchange and access to academic expertise. Approximately 10 EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are expected to be offered across the UK during the 2026–2027 programme cycle, with applications closing at midday on 8 October 2026 . About the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Programme The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship programme has been created to increase the number, capacity and diversity of Policy Fellowship opportunities available across the United Kingdom. Through the programme, research organisations can receive financial and practical support to establish and deliver fellowships that connect researchers with UK public and civil servants. Research organisations selected as hosts will be responsible for developing programmes that allow participating public and civil servants to spend meaningful time engaging with researchers and exploring specific policy questions and challenges. Policy Fellows can be selected from any public bodies and across all levels of seniority . The programme is intended to provide participating public and civil servants with opportunities to: Explore specific policy challenges and questions with relevant researchers. Access specialist academic and research expertise. Develop new approaches to problem-solving. Build relationships between researchers and policymakers. Expand professional networks. Participate in professional development and knowledge-exchange activities. Explore policy issues through interdisciplinary academic perspectives. The Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are specifically intended to create additional capacity and diversity by supporting research organisations outside the existing EvEx consortium to establish their own Policy Fellowship programmes. This funding call is complementary to EvEx s separate call for individual and small-team Policy Fellows, which is administered and hosted directly by the EvEx consortium. Funding Available Through the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Eligible organisations may apply for a maximum budget of £62,500 to deliver their proposed Associate Policy Fellowship programme. EvEx suggests that organisations use the funding to offer approximately three to 10 Associate Policy Fellowships . However, the programme also allows some flexibility in how organisations design their fellowship activities. EvEx is open to proposals that use alternative approaches to engaging Associate Policy Fellows, provided that participating public or civil servants spend a minimum of five days during the five-month programme period exploring policy questions with research input from one or more participating research organisations. This flexibility gives organisations the opportunity to develop a fellowship model suited to their institutional strengths, available expertise and the policy challenges they want to address. When Will the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowships Take Place? Successful host organisations will deliver their Associate Policy Fellowship programmes between January and May 2027 . Policy Fellows must spend a minimum of five days engaging with researchers at the host organisation or organisations during this five-month period. For the standard fellowship model, Fellows or Fellowship teams will spend a minimum of five days in person at a university or universities, with those days distributed across January to May 2027. The programme does not necessarily require Fellows to complete all five days consecutively. Instead, host organisations will need to design a programme that best meets the needs of their Fellows and the policy questions being explored. What Can an Associate Policy Fellowship Include? Each successful host organisation will be responsible for designing a programme that responds appropriately to its Fellows policy needs. Activities may include: 1. Meetings Between Policy Fellows and Researchers Policy Fellows can meet directly with researchers to discuss particular policy questions, challenges or areas where specialist knowledge would be valuable. These engagements may take the form of individual meetings between a Fellow and a researcher or broader interdisciplinary discussions involving researchers from several fields. Roundtable discussions may also be used to bring different academic perspectives to a policy problem. 2. Participation in Relevant Seminars and Events Policy Fellows may participate in seminars, workshops, lectures or other relevant events taking place at the host university or research organisation. This can provide Fellows with additional exposure to emerging research, specialist expertise and wider academic conversations related to their policy responsibilities. 3. Professional and Institutional Network Building Host organisations can use the Fellowship programme to establish stronger connections between participating public and civil servants and the research community. These relationships can help facilitate longer-term knowledge exchange and potentially create future opportunities for collaboration between policymakers and researchers. Who Can Apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards? The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards are open to research organisations in the United Kingdom that are eligible for UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) funding . Eligible organisations may include: Universities. Colleges. Research centres. Research institutes. Public sector research establishments. Other eligible independent research organisations. Importantly, organisations do not need previous experience running Policy Fellowships . EvEx specifically encourages applications from organisations that have never previously offered Policy Fellowships, as well as organisations that already have experience delivering similar programmes. Groups of research organisations are also permitted to apply together and jointly operate an Associate Policy Fellowship programme. Do Organisations Need to Have Policy Fellows Identified Before Applying? No. Applicants do not need to know who their prospective Policy Fellows will be when submitting their proposal. Successful organisations can subsequently operate an open application process through which eligible Policy Fellows can apply. The EvEx team can provide support and help amplify these recruitment opportunities. This means organisations interested in establishing a programme should not be discouraged from applying simply because they have not already identified specific public or civil servants to participate. Can Organisations Propose a Specific Fellowship Theme? Yes. Applicants may design their proposed Fellowships around a particular theme or policy topic. However, EvEx advises organisations to consider avoiding themes that are excessively narrow, as broader themes may provide greater flexibility when recruiting Fellows and matching them with appropriate researchers. Organisations uncertain about whether their proposed theme is suitable are encouraged to contact the EvEx team before submitting their application. Who Can Participate as an EvEx Associate Policy Fellow? For this programme, Policy Fellows are UK public and civil servants . Host organisations can recruit individuals from different public bodies and at different levels of seniority. Fellowships may be offered to: Individual public or civil servants. Small teams from the public or civil service. Participants from different public bodies. Participants across different levels of professional seniority. Each Fellow or Fellowship team should engage with researchers for at least five days during the January–May 2027 programme period. Benefits for Successful Host Organisations The programme provides more than financial support. Organisations receiving an EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Award will participate in a dedicated Coaching and Learning Programme designed to support them in developing and delivering effective Policy Fellowship programmes. Successful hosts will receive assistance covering important stages of fellowship delivery. Support From the EvEx Team The EvEx team will provide advice and guidance on designing and delivering a Policy Fellowship programme. Support can cover areas including: Selecting and recruiting Fellows. Matching Policy Fellows with appropriate researchers. Designing fellowship activities. Managing Fellows time within participating institutions. Developing effective approaches to knowledge exchange. Application and Documentation Templates Successful host organisations will receive access to template application forms and other documentation. These resources can be used directly or adapted to suit an organisation s individual recruitment and programme requirements. Coaching and Learning Support Host teams will have access to ongoing assistance from a Coaching and Learning Consultant . This will include: Training. Facilitated workshops. Specially developed shared resources. Practical guidance for Fellowship delivery. Knowledge Exchange Between Host Organisations Successful organisations will also have opportunities to interact with other participating hosts. This provides an additional platform for sharing experiences, exchanging ideas and discussing best practices for running effective Policy Fellowship programmes. Longer-Term Organisational Benefits Running an Associate Policy Fellowship programme can also help participating institutions develop stronger relationships with policymakers and public sector professionals. Potential organisational benefits highlighted by EvEx include: Building networks of public and civil servants. Establishing connections between public sector professionals and researchers. Strengthening institutional policy engagement. Developing the skills of staff responsible for managing Policy Fellowships. Accessing training, workshops and shared learning resources. Creating opportunities to demonstrate case studies and impacts resulting from policy-to-research engagement. Policy Fellows recruited through participating organisations will also be invited to join the wider EvEx Policy Fellows network , through which they can receive invitations to relevant networking activities and events. EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 Timeline Applicants should take note of the following key dates: 1 September 2026: Applications open. 9 September 2026: Online information session for prospective applicants. 8 October 2026: Application deadline. By 30 October 2026: Applicants expected to be notified of outcomes. Late January 2027: Fellowships begin. March 2027: Interim report submitted. By 31 May 2027: Fellowships completed. 30 June 2027: Final report submitted. The source also lists By 11 January 2026 – EvEx Policy Fellows recruited. This appears chronologically inconsistent with the surrounding 2027 programme dates, so prospective applicants should refer to the official guidance or confirm the intended year directly with EvEx rather than assuming a correction. Application Deadline The deadline to apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards is midday on 8 October 2026 . Applications opened on 1 September 2026 . Applicants are strongly encouraged to prepare their proposals early and carefully review the official guidance before completing the online application. Online Information Session for Applicants EvEx will host an online information session for prospective applicants on: 9 September 2026 at 1:30 p.m. The webinar will provide an opportunity to learn more about the Policy Fellowships and ask questions about either the Fellowship model or the application process. Prospective applicants can register for the session through the official EvEx website. How to Apply for the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship Organisations interested in applying should first review the complete programme guidance and application form provided by EvEx. Applicants can then prepare their proposal and submit the final application using the online application form available through the EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship webpage . The application guidance and a downloadable application form are available to help organisations prepare their responses before completing the online submission. Applicants are also encouraged to discuss their proposed project with the EvEx team before submitting an application. This provides an opportunity to check whether the proposed organisation and programme meet the scheme s eligibility requirements and intended scope. Applicants wishing to arrange a discussion can contact Christina Rozeik and the EvEx team at evex@csap.cam.ac.uk . Applications may also be submitted in Welsh. Welsh-language guidance is available, and applicants who want the application form in Welsh can request it directly from the EvEx team. APPLY NOW Reporting Requirements for Successful Organisations Successful organisations will be required to report on their Fellowship activities and expenditure at two key stages. Interim Report – March 2027 Around the midpoint of the programme, participating organisations will complete an interim reporting form. The interim report is expected to cover: Information about the EvEx Policy Fellows recruited. Progress achieved to date. Programme activities undertaken. Budget expenditure. Final Report – June 2027 Following completion of the Fellowship programme, host organisations will submit a final report. The report will request fuller information concerning: Delivery of the programme. Overall expenditure. Activities undertaken. Outcomes and impacts that have emerged from the programme. The source states that the final report is due 30 June 2027 . How Many Hosting Awards Are Available? For the 2026–2027 programme , EvEx expects to offer approximately 10 Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards across the United Kingdom . Because the number of awards is limited, eligible organisations interested in participating should carefully develop proposals that demonstrate how their Fellowship programme can create meaningful engagement between researchers and public or civil servants. About Evidence Exchange (EvEx) Evidence Exchange, or EvEx, is supporting stronger connections between research and policymaking through initiatives such as the Associate Policy Fellowship programme. The programme is funded by the Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC) and delivered by the Centre for Science and Policy (CSaP) at the University of Cambridge , together with partners across the United Kingdom. Through the Associate Policy Fellowship Hosting Awards, EvEx aims to expand Policy Fellowship opportunities beyond its existing consortium and help additional research organisations develop the capacity, expertise and networks required to engage effectively with policymakers. Conclusion The EvEx Associate Policy Fellowship 2027 represents a substantial opportunity for UK research organisations seeking to strengthen connections between academic research and public policymaking. With funding of up to £62,500 , successful organisations can establish programmes that bring UK public and civil servants into closer engagement with researchers, creating space to explore real policy challenges, access specialist expertise, develop professional networks and strengthen knowledge exchange. The opportunity is particularly accessible because applicants do not need previous experience running Policy Fellowships, and organisations can receive extensive practical support through EvEx s Coaching and Learning Programme. Universities and other eligible research organisations may also collaborate and submit joint proposals. Approximately 10 hosting awards are expected to be available during the 2026–2027 cycle. Eligible UK research organisations interested in applying should review the official programme guidance, consider attending the 9 September 2026 information session , and prepare their proposal ahead of the final application deadline. Application Deadline: Midday, 8 October 2026. Visit the OFY website for more Grant and Fellowship opportunities.
